question.text: Which of the following is a key SEBI requirement for a Category III AIF that uses substantial leverage and short positions?

answer.text: Leverage must NOT exceed 2x of NAV; regulatory reporting (monthly/quarterly) of leverage and exposure.
Leverage is unlimited if disclosed in PPM.
Short selling is banned for Cat III AIFs.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** SEBI caps Cat III leverage at 2x of NAV and mandates periodic (at least monthly/quarterly, per regulations) exposure + leverage reporting. Essential for systemic-risk monitoring. **The Trap:** B, C, D all misstate the regulatory regime. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C, XIX-B cover same leverage/reporting rules. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Build a daily leverage dashboard even though regulatory reporting is monthly — SEBI spot-checks and auditor queries can ask for any historical day. A 2-year lookup on leverage by day is standard; use the prime-broker margin file as the source of record.
